text:
eli: Heads up — saw 3x OOMs on canary after the kernel-routing change. Quick profiler dump below, looks tied to workspace peak growth when batched decode + KV cache warmup hit together. Anyone else seeing this?

dev-bot: deploy: rt-kernel-routing v2 -> canary :rocket:

eli: Profiler highlights (very rough):
```
peak_alloc_mb: before=6400  after=9800
hot_ops: kv_prefetch, attn_kern_shim, continuous_batcher
workspace_reserved_per_stream: ~2.5GB
fragmentation_est: high (many small free segments after splits)
```

mira: ugh. that lines up with the alloc-fuzz traces i pulled last night. when the KV warmup prefetches long prefixes we end up splitting lots of slabs and small leftover slices never get coalesced.

sam: did we change any allocator knobs in that rollout? expandable_segments, max_split_size_mb, garbage_collection_threshold, etc?

eli: not in the rollout — but experiment notes show defaults: expandable_segments=true, max_split_size_mb=256, garbage_collection_threshold=0.75.

mira: quick hypothesis: expandable_segments + large max_split_size_mb leads to aggressive splits and a stew of small fragments under mixed sequence length workloads. lowering max_split_size_mb or disabling expandable_segments should reduce fragmentation.

sam: sounds plausible. any numbers from a quick A/B?

mira: did a short backtest on an A100-80GB canary VM:
```
ctrl (defaults): 1000 requests -> 3 OOMs, 1.0x tokens/sec
A: max_split_size_mb=128 -> 1000 reqs -> 0 OOMs, tokens/sec 0.99x
B: expandable_segments=false -> 1000 reqs -> 1 OOM, tokens/sec 0.98x
C: gc_threshold=0.6 -> 1000 reqs -> 0 OOMs, tokens/sec 0.995x
```
so lowering max_split_size_mb and nudging GC threshold helped the most in this tiny run.

eli: nice. Did you check KV cache memory accounting — are we double-counting reserved vs used?

mira: KV accounting seems fine; issue is ephemeral workspace + leftover fragments from split. also the batching heuristic increases prefix sizes due to coalesced requests which makes the peak burst bigger.

sam: two followups: 1) we should try a combo run (max_split_size_mb=128 + gc_threshold=0.6 + expandable_segments=true) 2) add a temporary flag to toggle these per-model so we can A/B traffic on canary. I'll add the flag.

dev-bot: latency-bot: tail latency +95th bumped ~5% on canary after rt-kernel-routing v2 (observed at 14:02 UTC).

eli: ok we need to watch tradeoffs — lowering max_split_size_mb might increase internal copy churn but if it prevents OOMs it's worth it. can we measure tail-latency impact in the combo?

mira: yes i'll run combo and capture per-token latency and tail percentiles. plan:
- run 10k batched decodes with realistic kv-prefix distribution
- combos: ctrl, A, B, A+B+C
- gather: peak_alloc, fragmentation sketch, tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99
I'll post results here.

sam: i'll wire a model-level knob and a canary rollout path. also adding an opt-in to disable prefetch for long prefixes (kv_prefetch_limit=2048 tokens) to see if reducing prefetch reduces bursts.

eli: cool. TL;DR action items: @mira run ablation and post numbers; @sam add feature-flag for allocator knobs + kv_prefetch_limit; roll combo to canary and watch latency-bot and OOM counts.

mira: started the ablation now, ETA ~2h. will paste csv + flamegraph links (dashboard: https://ui.internal.redwood/perf/canary/2820001122)

sam: added flag in canary branch, PR up: https://git.internal/redwood/rt/compare/knob-canary (opt-in only).

eli: great, thanks. If we can get a no-OOM config with <2% tail-latency regress we can promote. If not, we should revert the kernel-routing change behind a rollback flag.

mira: results in ~90m, pinging here when done. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
